docRequirement: hooks.md § Common input fields binds `effort` as a common hook input field: "Object with a `level` field holding the active effort level for the turn: `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, or `"max"`", "If the requested model effort exceeds what the current model supports, this is the downgraded level the model actually used", "Present for events that fire within a tool-use context, such as `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `SubagentStop`, when the current model supports the effort parameter. The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable." (hooks.md:637). Three obligations: (a) the JSON a hook reads on stdin carries `effort.level`; (b) a hook command's process environment carries `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`; (c) a Bash tool call's process environment carries `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`. The spelling `CLAUDE_EFFORT` is the one the page gives; it gives no other.
current:

divergence:
Not a key-name problem and not a wrong value: the hooks subsystem is never handed the effort at all. Three separate absences behind one doc sentence.

1. INPUT FIELD ABSENT. `effort` is not on `SdkAutomationInput` (types.ts:742-901), so `effort.level` cannot appear on hook stdin or in `NESSY_EVENT_DATA`. Note the documented shape is an OBJECT with a `level` field, not a bare string — a fix that sets `effort: "high"` would satisfy a grep and still break `jq -r '.effort.level'`.

2. ENV VAR ABSENT FOR HOOKS. `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46-81) mirrors a closed list of fourteen fields and would not emit an effort variable even once the input carries one. The documented spelling is `CLAUDE_EFFORT`; this builder emits no `CLAUDE_*` key of its own today (Claude-spelled keys reach a hook only through `actionEnv` from `claudeCompatPluginEnv`, data-paths.ts:127-135), so this is also the first host-owned Claude-spelled variable it would produce. The fork's own precedent for that is the skills path, which emits BOTH spellings (runtime-skill-content.ts:136).

3. ENV VAR ABSENT FOR THE BASH TOOL. The doc's second clause ("and the Bash tool") has no implementation on either bash surface (pi-agent.ts:5191-5212, local-tools/runtime.ts:520). This half is independent of 1 and 2 — it is not fixed by fixing the hook input.

One thing is NOT divergent and must not be "fixed": the exec-form placeholder list (hook-command.ts:161-170) is deliberately closed to documented PATH placeholders. hooks.md:637 calls `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` an environment variable, not an exec-form placeholder, and exec form documents that `$`-forms pass through verbatim, so `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` staying literal in an `args` element is correct behaviour.

blastRadius:
Four consumers, one externally observable contract, no persistence change.

- `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46) has four call sites across two packages: the in-process spawn (hook-command.ts:664), the host's sandboxed plugin-hook runner (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4344), and the public re-export (packages/shared/src/automations/index.ts:129). Both hook execution authorities change at once, which is the point — they must not disagree.
- HOOK STDIN / ENV IS AN EXTERNAL CONTRACT (the risk trigger here). The same JSON goes to third-party hook processes imported from Claude and Codex plugin bundles via `hookCommandStdinPayload` (hook-command.ts:641, SessionManager.ts:4488) and via `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` (hook-command.ts:53). Adding a field and two env keys is additive and no hook can regress on it, but it IS visible outside the process. No persistence boundary is crossed: nothing here is written to disk, and no session/config schema changes.
- `SdkAutomationInput` is the single input type for both matcher adapters and every backend — `matcherMatchesSdk`/`getMatchValueForSdkInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts), `AutomationSystem.executeAgentEvent` (packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:629) on the native path, and `executePluginHookAutomations` on the plugin path. `effort` is not a matcher field on any event, so no matcher behaviour changes.
- CLAUDE-SDK PATH, already partly live: the SDK hook callback spreads the SDK's own input verbatim (`{...input, hook_event_name, tool_use_id}`, packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1643-1646). If the upstream Claude Agent SDK supplies `effort`, that object already reaches stdin today on the Claude backend (opt-in, `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` off by default) — which is why step 2 must let the call site win over the injected value. `AutomationSystem.buildSdkHooks()` returns `{}` (automation-system.ts:814), so native automations never take that path.
- BASH ENV: `pi-agent.ts:5212` feeds `config.processSupervisorPort.start(...)`, which serves every supervised child — the Bash tool, plugin `bin/` invocations, and skill-context commands (SessionManager.ts:4700). A new variable there is visible to every user command. The `process_start_request` wire shape (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:449, :3664) is NOT touched.
- TESTS THAT PIN NEARBY BEHAVIOUR: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.plugin-hook-runners.test.ts:189` asserts the runner's source text contains the exact `stdinData: hookCommandStdinPayload(options.event, options.input, authorizedCwd)` line — unaffected unless that line is reformatted. `packages/shared/src/automations/task-hooks.test.ts:135-153` asserts the NESSY_* mirrors reach a real spawned hook and is the closest existing harness to copy for a live-env test. `packages/shared/src/automations/sdk-bridge.test.ts` pins the dead sibling builder.
- `packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts` gains a second consumer of `clampThinkingLevelToModel` (today only the agent path). `ThinkingLevel` has 88 callers; nothing there changes because the new type is a separate five-value alias in automations/.
userImpact:
Narrow but real, and silent when it bites — on the default Pi runtime, today.

A user writes (or installs a Claude plugin that ships) a `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop`/`SubagentStop` hook that branches on effort — the documented use is exactly that, e.g. requiring approval for expensive tools only at low effort, or tagging an audit log with the level the turn actually ran at. Both documented ways of reading it come back empty: `jq -r '.effort.level'` over the stdin payload yields `null`, and `echo "$CLAUDE_EFFORT"` inside the hook prints nothing. The hook does not error and does not warn — it takes the unset branch, so a policy hook meant to tighten at low effort silently never tightens. Same for a Bash tool call: `echo $CLAUDE_EFFORT` in any command the model runs prints empty.

This is not surfaced anywhere. Unlike the ConfigChange matcher case there is no `matcher_never_matches`-style registration diagnostic for a missing input field, so nothing tells the hook author the field will always be absent.

One partial exception, unverified and off by default: on the Claude backend (`NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`), a plugin hook's stdin JSON is the SDK's own input object spread verbatim (hooks-automation.ts:1643-1646), so `effort.level` may already arrive there. `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` is still never set on that path, because the env builder mirrors a closed field list.
notes:
Effort rationale, since it touches two packages: five production files, but every edit is small (two lines in the env builder, one field on the input type, one helper plus one merge in BaseAgent, one property at the SubagentStop emitter, one env entry in the process-start handler) and none crosses a wire or persistence boundary — the `process_start_request` message shape and all session/config schemas are untouched. Called M rather than L on that basis; the only cross-package touch is a single added property in packages/server-core.

Correction carried from the challenger and re-verified here: the filed state said "thirteen NESSY_* field mirrors"; hook-command.ts:61-74 is FOURTEEN (TOOL_NAME, TOOL_INPUT, TOOL_RESPONSE, ERROR, PROMPT, SOURCE, MODEL, AGENT_ID, AGENT_TYPE, TASK_ID, TASK_SUBJECT, TASK_DESCRIPTION, MESSAGE, TITLE). Cosmetic; the conclusion is unchanged.

Sibling-subsystem check (the classic wrong answer here). Three near-misses, all read: (1) `buildEnvFromSdkInput` (packages/shared/src/automations/sdk-bridge.ts:15) is an identically-purposed env builder in the SAME subsystem that has NO production caller — patching it proves nothing; the live builder is `buildHookCommandEnv`. (2) The `effort` that DOES work is the SKILLS one (runtime-skill-content.ts:136, base-agent.ts:2201-2208, skills.md:299) — the finding names that sibling correctly and is about hooks. (3) `applySkillInvocationEffort` (base-agent.ts:2625) mutates `_thinkingLevel` for one turn, so any effort snapshot must be read per event, not cached at session start.

Absence claims all made with `grep -a` per the NUL-byte trap: `grep -ran 'CLAUDE_EFFORT\|NESSY_EFFORT'` over packages/ and apps/ excluding dist/ returns five files, none of them in automations/, plugins/ or the process-start path; `grep -an effort packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts` returns zero hits in the entire file.

Not an owner decision: `effort` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` appear in none of the nine dated decisions indexed in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and this is not a de-brand or dropped-subscription difference — the fork already implements the identical variable for skills citing skills.md:299, so the hook/Bash half is an unimplemented contract rather than a deliberate omission.

TWO THINGS I DID NOT VERIFY, neither load-bearing for the divergence. (a) Whether the upstream Claude Agent SDK actually populates `effort` on its hook inputs — it would only affect the opt-in Claude backend, and `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` is absent there regardless; the recommended merge order in change step 2 is written so that either answer is safe. (b) Whether the process supervisor merges `env` over the host environment rather than replacing it — I read the assertion in the comment at pi-agent.ts:5184-5186 and the PATH-rebuild code that depends on it, but not the supervisor implementation itself. If it replaced rather than merged, the Bash-tool edit would need a different seam; the hook halves are unaffected either way.

One non-defect worth stating so it is not "fixed": hooks.md:637 calls `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` an environment variable, and hooks.md § Exec form and shell form documents `$`-forms as passing through verbatim in exec form. Adding EFFORT to `EXEC_FORM_PATH_PLACEHOLDERS` (hook-command.ts:161-170) would therefore make us diverge, not converge.
